title: 2018 AMC 10B Problem 22
statement: Real numbers \(x\) and \(y\) are chosen independently and uniformly at random from the interval \([0, 1].\) Which of the following numbers is closest to the probability that \(x,\) \(y,\) and \(1\) are the side lengths of an obtuse triangle?

solutions.text: The three lengths \(x, y, 1\) make a triangle iff \(x + y > 1.\) Since \(1\) is the longest side, that triangle is obtuse iff \(x^2 + y^2 < 1.\) So in the unit square we want the region inside the quarter circle \(x^2 + y^2 = 1\) but above the line \(x + y = 1.\) That’s the quarter disk with the right triangle under the chord removed: \(\tfrac{\pi}{4} - \tfrac12 \approx 0.285.\) The closest choice is \(0.29.\) Therefore, the answer is C.
hints: A triangle with sides \(x, y, 1\) needs \(x + y > 1;\) since \(1\) is the longest side it is obtuse when \(x^2 + y^2 < 1\)
In the unit square this region is a quarter disk with the triangle below \(x + y = 1\) removed
